Keywords: history, monthly, daily, rising, falling, line, time series, trend
Secondary Options: Area chart; step line; sparkline
When to Use: One to five measures sampled at regular times where the shape of the movement matters more than each exact value.
When NOT to Use: Fewer than four points (show the numbers), many series that tangle, or categories with no order.
Accessibility Notes: Do not rely on hue alone: vary dash style and label the lines directly at their ends. Offer the same numbers in a table and state the headline change in text.

Keywords: compare, categories, bar, ranking, sales by region, survey, counts
Secondary Options: Vertical column chart; lollipop; dot plot
When to Use: Comparing one value across a handful to a few dozen named groups, especially when labels are long.
When NOT to Use: Time series (use a line) or parts of a whole that must sum to a total.
Accessibility Notes: Start the axis at zero, sort by value, put the value on the bar, and make bars distinguishable from the background at 3:1.

Keywords: share, proportion, composition, percentage, pie, donut, budget
Secondary Options: Donut with two to four slices; treemap; waffle
When to Use: Showing how one total divides when there are few parts and the point is which is largest.
When NOT to Use: More than five slices, parts that do not add to a whole, or comparing several totals.
Accessibility Notes: Label every slice with its name and value so colour is not the key; order from largest; give a table with the same parts.

Keywords: correlation, scatter, relationship, outlier, regression, two variables
Secondary Options: Bubble chart; hexbin; connected scatter
When to Use: Two numeric measures for many items, to see clusters, trends and outliers.
When NOT to Use: Few items, or when one axis is categories.
Accessibility Notes: Vary marker shape as well as colour; supply a text summary of the correlation; allow keyboard focus on points for dense plots via a table.

Keywords: distribution, histogram, box plot, spread, median, quartile, frequency
Secondary Options: Box plot; violin; density plot; strip plot
When to Use: Showing how values spread, where they bunch and where the outliers are.
When NOT to Use: A handful of values, or when exact figures matter more than shape.
Accessibility Notes: State the bin width, mark the median with a label, and give summary figures (min, median, max) in text.

Keywords: heatmap, matrix, intensity, hour by day, correlation matrix, grid
Secondary Options: Calendar heatmap; table with cell shading
When to Use: A value across two category axes, when patterns by row, column or block are the story.
When NOT to Use: When exact values are needed, or the grid is too large to read.
Accessibility Notes: Use a sequential colour scale that holds contrast in greyscale, print the value in each cell if it fits, and give a table fallback.

Keywords: map, choropleth, region, location, geography, markers, country
Secondary Options: Proportional symbol map; tile map; cartogram
When to Use: Values that belong to places, where position helps people find their own area.
When NOT to Use: When regions differ hugely in size and the number is a count (use a rate), or the places carry no pattern.
Accessibility Notes: A map is not accessible alone: pair it with a ranked list of regions, label key places, and avoid red and green as the only contrast.

Keywords: funnel, conversion, drop-off, stages, pipeline, checkout steps
Secondary Options: Stepped column chart; Sankey for branches
When to Use: Ordered stages where each stage can only hold what the previous one passed on.
When NOT to Use: Stages that can be entered in any order.
Accessibility Notes: Show count and percentage retained on each stage as text, keep stage names visible without hover, and describe the largest drop in a sentence.

Keywords: sankey, flow, transfer, movement, source to destination, journey, energy
Secondary Options: Alluvial diagram; chord diagram; table of flows
When to Use: Quantities moving from sources to destinations through steps, where the width of the link is the amount.
When NOT to Use: Cyclic flows, or when there are more than about a dozen nodes.
Accessibility Notes: Label nodes and link values directly, support keyboard focus per node, and list the largest flows in a table.

Keywords: target, goal, bullet chart, progress, quota, KPI, budget vs actual
Secondary Options: Bar with target line; progress bar
When to Use: One measure compared with a goal and bands such as poor, fair and good.
When NOT to Use: Many items with different units.
Accessibility Notes: Mark the target with a line and a text label, not only colour; state the percentage reached as text.

Keywords: forecast, prediction, confidence interval, projection, range, scenario
Secondary Options: Fan chart; dashed projection line
When to Use: A history followed by a projection where the range of likely values should be seen.
When NOT to Use: When the model gives only one number and no error estimate.
Accessibility Notes: Use a dashed line and a distinct label for projected values, explain what the band means in a caption, and give lower and upper bounds in a table.

Keywords: anomaly, outlier, spike, alert, threshold, detection, incident
Secondary Options: Control chart; scatter with threshold line
When to Use: A series where a few points break the pattern and need attention.
When NOT to Use: When there are too many flagged points to discuss one by one.
Accessibility Notes: Mark anomalies with shape and text label, not colour alone; list the flagged points with dates and values.

Keywords: hierarchy, treemap, tree, nested, folder size, sunburst, portfolio
Secondary Options: Sunburst; indented tree list; icicle
When to Use: Part-to-whole across levels, where area shows size and nesting shows category.
When NOT to Use: When precise comparison between small items matters.
Accessibility Notes: Offer the hierarchy as a nested list, label rectangles that are large enough and show the rest in a tooltip that also opens on focus.

Keywords: process, workflow, steps, stages, diagram, swimlane, timeline of states
Secondary Options: Swimlane; state diagram; step list
When to Use: How work moves through ordered steps and decisions.
When NOT to Use: Quantities of flow (use a Sankey) or very long processes.
Accessibility Notes: Make it a real ordered list or an SVG with a title and description; do not export it only as an image.

Data Type: Running total with gains and losses
Keywords: waterfall, cumulative, bridge, variance, profit walk, increase decrease
Secondary Options: Stacked bar with connectors
When to Use: How an opening figure became a closing one through positive and negative steps.
When NOT to Use: When there are dozens of steps.
Accessibility Notes: Differentiate gains and losses with sign, label, and pattern as well as colour; read out start, each step and end in a table.

Keywords: radar, multivariate, profile, parallel coordinates, spider, scorecard
Secondary Options: Parallel coordinates; dot matrix; radar for three to six axes
When to Use: Comparing a few items on several measures with different scales.
When NOT to Use: Radar for many items (the shapes overlap), or when axes are unordered and misleading.
Accessibility Notes: Provide a table of scores, keep one shared scale for equal units and say so; avoid filled radars that hide each other.

Keywords: stock, OHLC, candlestick, trading, price, volume, financial
Secondary Options: OHLC bars; line with volume bars
When to Use: Open, high, low and close of a price per period for people who read price action.
When NOT to Use: Audiences who just want a trend (use a line).
Accessibility Notes: Do not rely on red and green: add fill style or arrows; give an accessible table of latest values and key levels.

Keywords: network, graph, nodes, links, relationships, dependencies, social
Secondary Options: Adjacency matrix; arc diagram; list of edges
When to Use: Who or what connects to what, when the pattern of links matters.
When NOT to Use: Dense graphs with hundreds of nodes (a hairball), where a matrix reads better.
Accessibility Notes: Offer an adjacency list in text, enable keyboard navigation between nodes and name each node.

Data Type: Rankings and changes between two points
Keywords: slope chart, dumbbell, before after, rank change, two periods, difference
Secondary Options: Dumbbell plot; paired bars
When to Use: A before and after for many items, to see who rose and who fell.
When NOT to Use: More than two time points (use a line).
Accessibility Notes: Label both ends with values, use line style and arrows for direction, and give a table of start, end and change.

Keywords: KPI, big number, metric, stat card, headline, sparkline, summary
Secondary Options: Delta arrow; bullet; small bar
When to Use: One number that matters, with a small context of how it has moved.
When NOT to Use: When the audience needs to compare many figures at once.
Accessibility Notes: Put value, unit, period and change in text first; the sparkline is decoration with an aria-hidden or short text alternative.

Keywords: progress, gauge, completion, percentage, meter, steps done
Secondary Options: Segmented bar; ring for one value
When to Use: One value toward 100 percent.
When NOT to Use: Many values (use bars) or precise reading (gauges are hard to read).
Accessibility Notes: Use the native progress or meter element or role=progressbar with aria-valuenow, and show the number as text.

Keywords: stacked area, share over time, mix, category growth, layered
Secondary Options: 100 percent stacked columns; small multiples
When to Use: How a total and its parts changed together over time with a few categories.
When NOT to Use: When individual parts must be compared precisely; upper layers are hard to read.
Accessibility Notes: Direct-label layers, keep a stable colour order, and provide a table of values per period.

Keywords: calendar, seasonality, day of week, hour of day, activity, cycle
Secondary Options: Radial clock; grid of small bars
When to Use: Patterns by weekday, hour or date, such as activity or footfall.
When NOT to Use: When absolute values matter more than patterns.
Accessibility Notes: Label weekdays and months; give the busiest and quietest periods in text; use a ramp that is readable in greyscale.

Keywords: streaming, real time, live data, monitoring, ticker, websocket
Secondary Options: Sparkline; gauge with history
When to Use: Metrics that arrive continuously and need a short recent window.
When NOT to Use: When the audience needs the full history in one view.
Accessibility Notes: Do not move content faster than people can read; give a pause control, and update a polite status region at a calm interval.

Keywords: gantt, timeline, schedule, task duration, project plan, roadmap
Secondary Options: Timeline; range bars
When to Use: Tasks with start and end dates and, where useful, dependencies.
When NOT to Use: Many hundred tasks (summarise first).
Accessibility Notes: Provide a list of tasks with dates; show dependencies by line and label; keep rows keyboard focusable.

Keywords: small multiples, facet, panel, per region, repeated chart, trellis
Secondary Options: Sparkline table; shared-axis panels
When to Use: The same chart repeated per group so shapes are compared side by side.
When NOT to Use: When groups are few enough to overlay.
Accessibility Notes: Use one scale across panels, a title on each, and a note on the shared axis.

Keywords: waffle, icon array, proportion, one in ten, risk, share of people
Secondary Options: Single stacked bar
When to Use: A share explained as a number of units out of a hundred, which is easy to grasp.
When NOT to Use: Small differences or more than three categories.
Accessibility Notes: Use shape or pattern as well as colour, and state the numbers in a caption.
